subject: Final Inflation Test Before Fed Meeting

WSB won't be published with markets closed tomorrow, but tune back in on Friday.Good morning! Here's the latest in trending:Huang scandal: Nvidia (NVDA) CEO has no succession plan. California AG will continue probe.Mega merger: SpaceX (SPCX) and Tesla (TSLA) directors to negotiate a potential $3.5T deal.Thanksgiving travel: The FAA tightens "Line Up and Wait" rules, raising flight delay concerns.

 Happy Thanksgiving! Many thanks to all of our Wall Street Breakfast readership as we go into the holiday season. WSB won't be published with markets closed tomorrow, but tune back in on Friday. 

 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending:

Huang scandal: Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO has no succession plan . California AG will  continue probe .

 Mega merger:  SpaceX ( SPCX ) and Tesla ( TSLA ) directors to negotiate a potential $3.5T deal.

 Thanksgiving travel:  The FAA tightens "Line Up and Wait" rules, raising flight delay concerns.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 What to expect 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
Markets are bracing for the final major inflation reading before the Federal Reserve's last meeting of 2026, with the data likely to cement the odds of a 25-basis-point interest rate hike next month. The second estimate for Q3 gross domestic product is also due later in the day.

 Persistent inflation: The Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge , is expected to have increased 3.8% Y/Y in October, heating up from September's 3.6%. On a month-over-month basis, PCE likely ticked up 0.3% from September's 0.5% rise. The core PCE Price Index, which excludes food and energy, is seen rising 3.2% Y/Y, compared to 3.1% in the prior month. Core PCE likely rose 0.3% M/M, the same rate as in September. October's Consumer Price Index report showed that inflation cooled, but not as much as hoped . This, along with a hot PCE report, would support the case for continued rate hikes. ING strategists said the consensus estimate of 0.3% M/M "is still too hot for the Fed and will keep a hawkish bias in place." Markets are currently pricing in a 97.5% chance of the Fed raising rates by 25 bps in December.

 Confidence boost:  Notably, the Conference Board on Tuesday said consumer confidence rallied in November to reach its highest level since January 2025. This was driven by optimism over the labor market and the economy following the midterm elections. While the bond market effectively ignored the consumer confidence report, ING strategists said the core PCE print should be a worry for Treasurys. "Energy prices have come off and can help to tame headline inflation rates ahead, that does little for core inflation rates, or, at the very least, it will take a bit longer to feed through (e.g. airfares)," they said. "Confirmation of these expectations should, by definition, not be a surprise. But we feel that confirmation will, in fact, be enough to abort the downtrend in yields."  Consumer confidence gap hits widest level since 2021 

 Bigger picture:  The initial estimate for Q3 GDP was an expansion of 3.4%, compared to Q2's 2.2% increase. According to SA analyst Amrita Roy, the best combination for markets to rally would be if PCE comes in cooler than expected, while GDP comes at target. "A combination of a hotter PCE and a strong GDP report will force the Fed to tighten monetary policy further, which will reignite selling pressure for equities, with the worst outcome being a hotter PCE with a soft GDP report," she warned.  BlackRock noted that the second GDP estimate will offer a check on the resilience of the broader economy beyond the AI boom. "We eye October PCE data to assess whether services inflation remains a key sticking point - and if the figures keep further Fed tightening in play," it said, adding that the Middle East energy shock's impact on inflation has peaked.
